mainTopic: Food prices and profit in ארץ ישראל, leaving the Land, and stories about רות, בעז and אברהם
overview: This amud opens with the last words of a ruling from the previous page about taking food out of ארץ ישראל. A ברייתא forbids buying and reselling basic foods in ארץ ישראל for profit, and the גמרא explains why רבי אלעזר בן עזריה could still profit from wine and oil. Another ברייתא forbids profiting 'twice' from eggs, and רב and שמואל disagree about what that means. The גמרא then teaches that a community cries out in prayer, even on שבת, when the price of its main product crashes badly. Next, a ברייתא rules when one may leave ארץ ישראל in a famine, and רבי שמעון limits this to someone who cannot afford food. The punishment of אלימלך and his sons, who left ארץ ישראל, supports this, and the גמרא brings a series of stories about רות, בעז (identified with the judge אבצן) and his sixty children. Finally, רב חנן בר רבא brings a list of teachings in the name of רב: the family of נחשון, the names of the mothers of famous figures, אברהם's ten years in prison, and the world's mourning when אברהם died, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words of the earlier ruling about moving food between provinces
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a ruling from the previous page about taking food out of ארץ ישראל: 'from province to province.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From one province to the next province.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a statement that began on the previous page. That statement dealt with taking food out of ארץ ישראל to סוריא, and these words speak about moving it from one province to the province right next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking food out of ארץ ישראל can make it scarce and expensive for the people living there. This phrase applies that discussion to moving food between neighboring provinces. It sets the stage for the next ברייתא, which also protects the food supply of ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A province or district (a Greek word)

phrases.english: From province to province.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page about moving food from the last province of ארץ ישראל to the nearest province of סוריא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהִיפַּרְכְיָא לְהִיפַּרְכְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earlier ruling about taking food out of ארץ ישראל is applied to moving it from one province to the next.

steps.title: No middleman profit from basic foods in the Land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that in ארץ ישראל one may not buy and resell basic foods like wine, oil, and flour for profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In ארץ ישראל, one may not make a profit from things that people need to live, such as wines, oils, and flours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that forbids acting as a middleman to earn money from basic foods in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a middleman buys food and resells it, the price goes up, and poor people suffer. So the farmers who grow these foods should sell them directly in the market. The rule only covers foods that are basic to life, called חיי נפש.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a profit, earning money (here, by buying and reselling)
Things needed to stay alive; basic foods

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not make a profit in ארץ ישראל
phrases.notes: He means buying from the grower and reselling at a higher price.

phrases.english: with things that people need to live,
such as wines, oils, and flours.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מִשְׂתַּכְּרִים בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that also protects the food supply of ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל, one may not act as a middleman for profit in basic foods such as wine, oil, and flour.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the Torah's monetary laws protect the poor from rising food prices.

steps.title: A report that a great sage profited from wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: There is a report that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה made a profit from wine and oil, which seems to go against the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה that he used to make a profit from wine and oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to clash with the ברייתא it just quoted. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists wine and oil by name as forbidden. Yet a famous sage profited from exactly these two items. The גמרא does not say 'קשיא' out loud, but the story works as a challenge that needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They said about him.' This introduces a report about a sage's behavior.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: They said about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה,
that he used to make a profit from wine and oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to contradict the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ban on profiting from wine and oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A great sage did exactly what the ברייתא forbids, so how could the ברייתא be right, or how could he do it?

steps.title: Why wine and oil were allowed for him
steps.stepSummary: For wine, he followed רבי יהודה. For oil, oil was plentiful where he lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: With wine, he held like רבי יהודה. With oil, in the place where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה lived, oil was common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a separate reason for each item: one reason for wine and another for oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine: רבי יהודה (בן בתירא) holds that wine is not treated as a basic need, because drinking it leads to bad behavior. So a rise in its price is not a problem. Oil: where he lived there was plenty of oil, so reselling it would not make it scarce or expensive. The ברייתא is still true; these are exceptions in how it applies.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place, in his area

phrases.english: With wine, he held like רבי יהודה;
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה בן בתירא from the previous page, who allows this with wine because drinking it leads to bad behavior.

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁמֶן – בְּאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: with oil, in the place of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
oil was common.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיַיִן – סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate answers: for wine he follows a different תנא, and for oil the local situation was different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה broke the ban on profiting from basic foods.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine is not counted as a basic need according to רבי יהודה, and oil was plentiful in his area, so there was no worry that prices would rise.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban only applies when reselling would raise the price of a real basic need. Wine (according to רבי יהודה) and plentiful oil fall outside that concern.

steps.title: No profiting twice from eggs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not make a profit 'twice' from eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not make a profit twice with eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, this time about eggs. Its wording, 'twice,' is unclear, and the next step explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eggs are also a basic food, so the Rabbis limited the profit people could make on them. But the word 'twice' can be understood in more than one way. This sets up the dispute in the next step.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not make a profit twice with eggs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מִשְׂתַּכְּרִין פַּעֲמַיִם בְּבֵיצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on the same theme of limiting profit on food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not profit 'twice' from eggs; the exact meaning is explained next.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree on what 'twice' means
steps.stepSummary: One says 'twice' means charging double the price. The other says it means one merchant selling to another merchant.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרי בר מרי said: רב and שמואל disagree about this. One said: one for two. And one said: a merchant to a merchant.
steps.whatsHappening: מרי בר מרי reports two ways to understand the egg ברייתא, one from רב and one from שמואל, without telling us who said which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: View one: 'twice' is about the amount. A seller may not charge double what he paid. View two: 'twice' is about the number of middlemen. A merchant who bought eggs may not sell them to another merchant, because two profits on the same eggs push the price up. He must sell directly to the customer.

keyTerms.meaning: One said (the גמרא does not tell us which sage)
Two for one, meaning double the price

phrases.english: מרי בר מרי said:
רב and שמואל disagree about it;
One said: two for one.
phrases.notes: He means you can't charge double what you paid for the eggs.

phrases.english: And one said: a merchant to a merchant.
phrases.notes: He means a merchant can't resell to another merchant; he must sell straight to the customer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָרִי בַּר מָרִי: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unclear word 'twice' in the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: you may not charge double the price for eggs. Other view: eggs may not pass from one merchant to another merchant.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Twice' can mean double the price (an amount limit) or two middlemen (a limit on how many hands the eggs pass through).
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which view belongs to רב and which to שמואל. Don't assume the first view is רב's just because his name comes first.

steps.title: Crying out in prayer when merchandise prices collapse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the community cries out in public prayer over merchandise, even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We cry out in prayer over merchandise, and even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, still on the topic of prices: when merchandise loses its value, the community prays for help, even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with prices that are too high. Here the problem is the opposite: prices that crash and ruin merchants. The words 'even on שבת' show how serious this is, since normally we do not cry out for our needs on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We cry out / sound the alarm in public prayer

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a collapse of the local economy is treated as a public emergency, like a famine.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We cry out in prayer over merchandise,
phrases.notes: He means merchandise whose price has dropped badly, so the sellers are losing their living.

phrases.english: and even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַתְרִיעִין עַל פְּרַקְמַטְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rules about profit on food to a related rule about price crashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A community cries out in prayer over merchandise whose price collapsed, even on שבת.

steps.title: Which merchandise the ruling means
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains: goods that are the main local trade, like linen in בבל and wine and oil in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For example, linen goods in בבל, and wine and oil in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains what kind of 'merchandise' the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every product counts. He gives examples of the main product each place lives off, so a crash in its price hurts the whole public, not just one person.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
such as linen goods in Babylonia,
and wine and oil in the Land of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the word פרקמטיא in the ברייתא of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling applies to the main local product: linen in בבל, wine and oil in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: How big the price drop must be
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף limits the ruling to a drop where something worth ten sells for six.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: And this is only when the price fell and stood at six for what was worth ten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a limit: the crying out is only for a big drop in price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small dip is normal business and is not an emergency. Only when goods worth ten sell for six, a loss of about forty percent, do we cry out.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten for six; what was worth ten sells for six

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
And this is only when it dropped in price and stood
at ten for six.
phrases.notes: Goods that used to sell for ten coins now sell for only six.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וְהוּא דְּזָל וְקָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the ברייתא: how severe the drop must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We cry out only when the price fell from ten to six.
steps.whatToRemember: We cry out over a price crash only for the main local product (רבי יוחנן) and only for a big drop of ten to six (רב יוסף).

steps.title: When one may leave ארץ ישראל in a famine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not leave ארץ ישראל unless two סאה of grain cost a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not leave ארץ ישראל for outside the land unless two סאה of grain cost a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about prices: leaving ארץ ישראל is forbidden unless food has become very expensive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living in ארץ ישראל is so important that a normal rise in prices is not a reason to leave. Only a famine-level price, two סאה for a סלע, allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin of fairly large value

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not leave the Land of Israel for outside the land,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָמְדוּ סָאתַיִם בְּסֶלַע.
phrases.english: unless two se'a of grain stood at a sela.
phrases.notes: This describes a very high, famine-level price for grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין יוֹצְאִין מֵאָרֶץ לְחוּץ לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on another price-related law: leaving ארץ ישראל during famine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may leave ארץ ישראל only if grain is at famine prices: two סאה for a סלע.

steps.title: רבי שמעון limits the permission to leave
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the permission applies only to someone who cannot afford food; one who can buy may not leave even at worse prices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: When is this? When he cannot find food to buy. But when he can find food to buy, even if one סאה costs a סלע, he may not leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון narrows the rule of the ברייתא: the price alone does not decide; what matters is whether this person can still buy food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to allow anyone to leave once prices hit two סאה per סלע. רבי שמעון says it only applies to someone who has no money to buy. If he can still buy, he must stay even when prices are double that, one סאה per סלע.

keyTerms.meaning: Finds to buy; is able to buy

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one סאה per סלע is cheaper; it is twice as expensive as two סאה per סלע. רבי שמעון means: even at a worse price, if you can afford food, stay.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: When is this?
When he cannot find food to buy,
phrases.notes: He means he has no money to buy, not that there is no food in the market.

phrases.english: but when he is able to find food to buy,
even if one se'a stood at a sela,
he may not leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אֵימָתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in the ברייתא of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one who cannot afford food may leave; one who can buy food must stay even at very high prices.

steps.title: אלימלך and his sons were punished for leaving
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that אלימלך, מחלון and כליון, great leaders, were punished for leaving ארץ ישראל, and brings a פסוק from רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רבי שמעון בן יוחאי used to say: אלימלך, מחלון and כליון were great men and leaders of their generation. Why were they punished? Because they left ארץ ישראל for outside the land, as it says: 'And the whole city was stirred about them, and they said: Is this נעמי?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי שמעון's strict view with a story: אלימלך's family left during a famine even though they could afford food, and they were punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכן' (and likewise) shows this backs up the previous step. These were wealthy leaders who could have bought food, so leaving was wrong for them, matching רבי שמעון's rule. The פסוק is brought as the source that they were punished.

keyTerms.meaning: The great men of the generation
The leaders / providers of the generation

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And so Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai used to say:
Elimelech, Mahlon and Chilion,
were great men of the generation,
and were leaders of the generation;
and why were they punished?
Because they left the Land of Israel for outside the land,
as it is said:
"And the whole city was stirred about them,
and they said: Is this Naomi?"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי שמעון's rule in step 11 with a story from רות.
steps.raayaObject: That one who can afford food may not leave ארץ ישראל even in a famine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The punishment of אלימלך, מחלון and כליון, hinted at in רות 1:19.

steps.title: What does 'Is this נעמי' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the words 'Is this נעמי?' show they were punished for leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'Is this נעמי?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the פסוק just quoted means, setting up רבי יצחק's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, the women are only surprised to see נעמי. It is not clear how this proves anything about punishment for leaving, so the גמרא asks for an explanation.

phrases.english: What is meant by "Is this Naomi"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״הֲזֹאת נָעֳמִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the פסוק in step 12 supports the claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the words 'Is this נעמי?' show punishment for leaving ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: See what happened to נעמי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains the women were saying: look at what happened to נעמי, who left ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: They said, 'Have you seen נעמי, who left ארץ ישראל for outside the land? Look what became of her!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question: the women's words were a comment on how badly things turned out for נעמי after she left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Is this נעמי?' is not just surprise. It means: this is what became of the woman who left ארץ ישראל, and she came back with nothing. This completes the proof that leaving brought punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: What happened to her? What became of her?

steps.whatToRemember: One may leave ארץ ישראל only in a real famine, and according to רבי שמעון only if he cannot afford food. אלימלך's family, who could afford it, were punished for leaving.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said: They said:
Have you seen Naomi,
who left the Land of Israel for outside the land?
What became of her?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמְרוּ: חֲזִיתֶם נָעֳמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The women meant: look what happened to נעמי because she left ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: בעז's wife died the day רות arrived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that on the day רות came to ארץ ישראל, בעז's wife died, and links this to a popular saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: On the very day that רות the Moabite came to ארץ ישראל, בעז's wife died. This matches what people say: before the dying person has even died, the one who will run his house is already standing ready.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds another teaching about the story of רות. He says that בעז's wife died on the same day רות arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the way was being prepared for רות to marry בעז from the moment she arrived. The folk saying expresses the same idea: the next person in charge of the house is already there before the old one is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: רות from מואב, who came to ארץ ישראל with נעמי
The relative of נעמי who married רות
And this is what people say (introduces a folk saying)
The one put in charge of his house

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
That day that Ruth the Moabite came

phrases.aramaic: לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, מֵתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל בֹּעַז.
phrases.english: to the Land of Israel, the wife of Boaz died.
And this is what people say:
Before the dying one has died,
the one who will be in charge of his house is already standing.
phrases.notes: Here that new head of the house is רות, who later becomes בעז's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching by the same רבי יצחק on the story of רות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעז's wife died on the day רות arrived in ארץ ישראל, preparing the way for their marriage.

steps.title: The judge אבצן is בעז
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא in the name of רב identifies the judge אבצן with בעז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: אבצן is בעז.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching connected to the story of רות: רב says the judge called אבצן in ספר שופטים is really בעז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a bare identification of two names as one person. It does not yet tell us what we gain from it, which sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A judge from בית לחם mentioned in ספר שופטים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
Ivtzan is Boaz.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of בעז with a new identification
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judge אבצן is the same person as בעז.

steps.title: What does this identification teach us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we gain from knowing that אבצן is בעז.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters that אבצן is בעז. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just knowing that two names are one person seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to know what lesson comes out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what new point a statement adds)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the point of the identification in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson comes from identifying אבצן with בעז

steps.title: בעז made 120 feasts for his children
steps.stepSummary: The identification fits another teaching of רב: בעז, as אבצן, made 120 wedding feasts for his children, based on the פסוק about אבצן's sixty children.
steps.simpleTranslation: It fits the other teaching of רבה בר רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: בעז made 120 feasts for his children, as it says: "And he had thirty sons, and thirty daughters he sent outside, and thirty daughters he brought in for his sons from outside, and he judged Israel seven years."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the identification explains a second teaching of רב. Since בעז is אבצן, the פסוק about אבצן's many children tells us about בעז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says אבצן had thirty sons and thirty daughters, sixty children in all. Because אבצן is בעז, we learn that בעז had sixty children and made many wedding feasts for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the other one (it goes together with another statement)
He sent outside (married his daughters off to other families)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִידַּךְ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא –
phrases.english: It goes with the other teaching of Rabba bar Rav Huna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: for Rabba bar Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים מִשְׁתָּאוֹת עָשָׂה בֹּעַז לְבָנָיו,
phrases.english: Boaz made one hundred and twenty feasts for his children,
as it says:
"And he had thirty sons,
and thirty daughters he sent outside,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁלֹשִׁים בָּנוֹת הֵבִיא לְבָנָיו מִן הַחוּץ,
phrases.english: and thirty daughters he brought in for his sons from outside,
and he judged Israel seven years."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִידַּךְ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The identification lets us apply the פסוק about אבצן's sixty children to בעז, who made 120 feasts for them.

steps.title: Two feasts per wedding, and מנוח was never invited
steps.stepSummary: The 120 comes from two feasts at each of the sixty weddings. בעז never invited the childless מנוח, reasoning that he could never return the invitation.
steps.simpleTranslation: For each and every child he made two feasts, one in the house of the father and one in the house of the father-in-law. To none of them did he invite מנוח. He said: He is a barren mule, how will he ever pay me back?
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues, explaining how sixty children make 120 feasts. It also adds that בעז never invited מנוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sixty weddings times two feasts each makes 120. בעז skipped מנוח because מנוח had no children, so there would never be a wedding where מנוח could invite him back.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who became the father of שמשון; his wife was childless for many years
A barren mule (a harsh way of calling someone childless)

phrases.aramaic: וּבְכׇל אַחַת וְאַחַת עָשָׂה שְׁנֵי מִשְׁתָּאוֹת –
phrases.english: And for each and every one he made two feasts,
one in his father's house,
and one in his father-in-law's house;
and to none of them did he invite Manoach.
He said: A barren mule,
with what will he pay me back?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְכׇל אַחַת וְאַחַת עָשָׂה שְׁנֵי מִשְׁתָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's teaching, explaining the number 120 and adding the מנוח detail
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two feasts per wedding for sixty children make 120; מנוח was left out because he was childless.

steps.title: All sixty children died in his lifetime
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that all of בעז's sixty children died during his life, and the גמרא brings a folk saying that one quick child is better than sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And all of them died in his lifetime. This matches what people say: The sixty you bore in your lifetime, why do you need those sixty? Make the effort and bear one who is quicker than sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a sad ending: every one of בעז's sixty children died while he was still alive. The גמרא then quotes a popular saying that fits this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who would not invite the childless מנוח ended up without his own sixty children. The saying teaches that one excellent child is worth more than sixty who do not last.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a teaching from the time of the תנאים)
Make the effort, go to the trouble

steps.whatToRemember: בעז is identified with אבצן. He made 120 wedding feasts for his sixty children but never invited the childless מנוח, and all sixty of his children died in his lifetime.

phrases.english: It was taught: And all of them died in his lifetime.
And this is what people say:
"The sixty that you bore in your lifetime,
those sixty, why do you need them?
Make the effort and bear one who is quicker than sixty.
phrases.notes: Literally 'bend yourself over,' meaning push yourself to get it done.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּאנָא: וְכוּלָּן מֵתוּ בְּחַיָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about the fate of the children mentioned in steps 18-19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of בעז's sixty children died in his lifetime; one quick child is worth more than sixty.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of key words, to help us remember the order of the teachings of רב חנן בר רבא that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: מלך, אברהם, ten years, when he died, He alone was exalted.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a list of code words so we can remember the teachings that are about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one teaching. 'מלך' points to אלימלך, 'אברהם' points to the names of the mothers, 'עשר שנים' points to the ten years אברהם spent in prison, and 'שנפטר' points to the day אברהם died (step 32). The last word, 'נתנשא לבדו', points to a teaching on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid: code words that help you remember the order of teachings

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Melech, Abraham,
ten years, when he died, He alone was exalted.)

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the בעז teachings to a new series of teachings by רב חנן בר רבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory list for the teachings of רב חנן בר רבא that follow

steps.title: Four figures in מגילת רות all descend from נחשון
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that אלימלך, שלמון, פלוני אלמוני and the father of נעמי were all descendants of נחשון בן עמינדב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: אלימלך, שלמון, פלוני אלמוני, and the father of נעמי were all descendants of נחשון בן עמינדב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us a family fact. Four people connected to the story of רות all came from the great family of נחשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחשון was the נשיא of שבט יהודה, so these were people from a family of great זכות. The next step asks why this matters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So-and-so': the unnamed relative in מגילת רות
The נשיא (leader) of שבט יהודה in the מדבר

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said that Rav said:
Elimelech, and Salmon,
and So-and-so, and Naomi's father,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן בְּנֵי נַחְשׁוֹן בֶּן עַמִּינָדָב הֵן.
phrases.english: all of them are descendants of Nachshon son of Amminadab.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching in the memory list ('מלך')
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלימלך, שלמון, פלוני אלמוני and the father of נעמי were all from נחשון

steps.title: Why does this family fact matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lesson we learn from knowing that they all came from נחשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what point רב is making with this family fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A family tree alone is not a lesson. The גמרא wants to know what we should learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is he teaching us?' A request to hear the point of a teaching

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the teaching in step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson comes from the family connection to נחשון

steps.title: זכות אבות does not protect one who leaves ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Even someone with זכות אבות loses its protection when he leaves ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ, as we see from אלימלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even a person who has זכות אבות does not have that merit protect him when he leaves ארץ ישראל for חוץ לארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. אלימלך came from a great family, yet he died after leaving ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אלימלך was a descendant of נחשון, he had strong זכות אבות. He still died in מואב. This shows that leaving ארץ ישראל cancels that protection.

keyTerms.meaning: The merit of one's ancestors, which can protect a person

steps.whatToRemember: Coming from a great family is not enough. Leaving ארץ ישראל without good reason can cancel the protection of זכות אבות.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ זְכוּת אָבוֹת,
phrases.english: that even one who has the merit of his ancestors,
it does not stand for him
when he goes out from the Land to outside the Land.
phrases.notes: This is talking about אלימלך, who left for מואב and died there (רות 1).

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ זְכוּת אָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that זכות אבות does not protect someone who leaves ארץ ישראל

steps.title: The names of the mothers of אברהם and המן
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that אברהם's mother was אמתלאי בת כרנבו and המן's mother was אמתלאי בת עורבתי. A memory aid helps us keep them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא also said in the name of רב: אברהם's mother was אמתלאי בת כרנבו. המן's mother was אמתלאי בת עורבתי. Your memory aid: טמא goes with טמא, טהור goes with טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second teaching in the list ('אברהם'). Both mothers had the same name, so the גמרא gives a trick to tell them apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עורבתי sounds like עורב (a raven), which is a טמא bird, so it goes with the wicked המן. כרנבו sounds like כר (a sheep), which is a טהור animal, so it goes with אברהם.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Chanan bar Rava said that Rav said:
The mother of Abraham was Amatlai daughter of Karnevo.
The mother of Haman was Amatlai daughter of Orevati.
And your memory aid: impure with impure, pure with pure.
phrases.notes: עורב (raven) is a טמא bird, so it goes with המן. כר (sheep) is טהור, so it goes with אברהם.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the same series ('אברהם' in the memory list)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names of the mothers of אברהם and המן

steps.title: The names of the mothers of דוד and שמשון, and שמשון's sister
steps.stepSummary: The list goes on: דוד's mother was נצבת בת עדאל, שמשון's mother was צללפונית, and his sister was נשיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד's mother was named נצבת בת עדאל. שמשון's mother was צללפונית, and his sister was נשיין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב keeps going with more names of women that the פסוקים do not mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the step before, this gives names that are missing from תנ"ך and come from a tradition. The next step asks why we need to know them.

phrases.aramaic: אִמֵּיהּ דְּדָוִד – נִצֶּבֶת בַּת עַדְאֵל שְׁמָהּ.
phrases.english: The mother of David, Natzevet daughter of Adael was her name.
The mother of Samson was Tzelelponit,
and his sister was Nashyan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִמֵּיהּ דְּדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of mothers' names
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names of the mothers of דוד and שמשון, and of שמשון's sister

steps.title: What difference do these names make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical use there is in knowing these names.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters to know names that the פסוקים do not even mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These names do not change any הלכה, so the גמרא asks what they are good for.

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the list of names
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it matters to know these names

steps.title: To answer the heretics
steps.stepSummary: Knowing the names lets us answer מינים who ask about details the פסוקים leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: For answering the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these names help us respond to מינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מין asks something like 'what was דוד's mother's name?' to mock the tradition, we can show that we have a tradition that gives the answer.

phrases.english: For an answer to the heretics.
phrases.notes: He means people who ask about details the פסוקים don't give. We can answer from our tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִתְשׁוּבַת הַמִּינִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names are useful for answering מינים

steps.title: אברהם was imprisoned for ten years
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that אברהם אבינו was in prison for ten years: three in כותא and seven in קרדו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא also said in the name of רב: אברהם אבינו was imprisoned for ten years, three in כותא and seven in קרדו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third teaching in the list ('עשר שנים'). It tells us how long אברהם was in prison and where.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten years are split between two places. The next step brings a different version of this split.

keyTerms.meaning: Two places where אברהם was held

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Chanan bar Rava said that Rav said:
For ten years our forefather Abraham was imprisoned:
three in Kuta, and seven in Kardu.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים נֶחְבַּשׁ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the series ('עשר שנים' in the memory list)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם was imprisoned for ten years: three in כותא and seven in קרדו

steps.title: רב דימי's reversed version
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי from נהרדעא teaches the numbers the other way around: seven years in כותא and three in קרדו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי of נהרדעא teaches it the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא reports the same teaching with the numbers switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree on ten years in total. They disagree only about which place had three years and which had seven.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Teaches it the opposite way': a reversed version of the teaching

phrases.english: And Rav Dimi of Neharde'a
teaches the opposite.
phrases.notes: He means seven years in כותא and three in קרדו.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא מַתְנִי אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the teaching in step 29
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven years in כותא and three in קרדו

steps.title: אור כשדים is a small area of כותא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא identifies the 'small passage of כותא' as אור כשדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The small passage of כותא is אור כשדים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a geography note that ties the prison in כותא to אור כשדים, the place named in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the prison story to the פסוק about אור כשדים, where אברהם came from (בראשית 11:31). רב חסדא says that a small part of כותא, its 'small passage', is the place the תורה calls אור כשדים.

keyTerms.meaning: Ur of the Chaldeans, the hometown of אברהם in the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: רב teaches that אברהם was imprisoned for ten years, part of it in כותא. רב חסדא adds that the small passage of כותא is אור כשדים.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The small passage of Kuta,
this is Ur Kasdim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא עִיבְרָא זְעֵירָא דְּכוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a place identification to the teaching about the prison in כותא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The small area of כותא is אור כשדים

steps.title: The world's leaders mourn אברהם on the day he died
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא quotes רב: on the day אברהם אבינו died, all the leaders of the nations stood in a line and said, 'Woe to the world that has lost...' The thought continues in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: On the day that אברהם אבינו passed away, all the great leaders of the nations of the world stood in a line, and they said: Woe to the world that has lost...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב about אברהם אבינו. This one describes how the leaders of the world mourned when he died, and it sets up the next line, which tells us what they said the world lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְאָמַר ('and he said') tells us this is part of the same chain of רב's teachings about אברהם, following his teaching about אברהם being in prison (step 29). The new point is that אברהם's importance was felt by the whole world, not only by his own family. The nations' leaders stood in a row the way mourners do, showing they felt a real loss.

keyTerms.meaning: the great leaders of the nations of the world
woe to it, an expression of mourning

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Chanan bar Rava says that Rav says:
On that day
when our forefather Avraham left the world,

phrases.aramaic: עָמְדוּ כׇּל גְּדוֹלֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּשׁוּרָה;
phrases.english: all the leaders of the nations of the world stood in a line,
phrases.notes: Standing in a line is how mourners stand, so they were acting like mourners.

phrases.english: and they said: Woe to the world that has lost

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching of רב about אברהם אבינו, moving from his early life (prison, אור כשדים) to the day he died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the day אברהם אבינו died, the leaders of all the nations stood in a line like mourners and lamented the world's loss.
